narration: Type I versus Type II error. Here's how to keep them apart.
A Type I error is rejecting H0 when it's actually true. Its probability is alpha, the cutoff you chose.
A Type II error is failing to reject an H0 that's false. Its probability is beta, and power, 1 − beta, is the chance of catching it.
